defects: The Epi hypothesis is placed on the wrong edge: produced puts `Epi h` on h : b ⟶ d, which is itself part of the square being concluded (f ≫ h = g ≫ k). In gold, the epi (`Epi f00x`) is on a transversal edge (M000 ⟶ M001) that is NOT part of the face being proved (xx1, on M001,M011,M101,M111); it goes from a vertex of the other given horizontal face into the source vertex of the missing face. This misplacement makes the produced statement false in general.

Concrete counterexample showing produced statement is not a theorem: work in Type/Set, take a' = b' = c' = d' a singleton, so sq_top, sq_left_front, sq_left_back, sq_right_front, sq_right_back all hold trivially (Hom(-, singleton) has one element) for any f,g,h,k. Choose h : b → d a bijection (hence Epi) but choose f,g,k so that f ≫ h ≠ g ≫ k (e.g. a=c=singleton, b=d={1,2}, f(1)=1,g(1)=1,h=id,k(1)=2). All 5 hypotheses and Epi h hold, but the conclusion CommSq f g h k fails — so the produced theorem as stated is false, hence not equivalent to the true gold statement.

The direction of the vertical edges (φ_a : a ⟶ a', etc., pointing from the concluded/unprimed square to the given/primed square) is opposite to gold's vertical edges (f00x etc., pointing from the given face's vertex M000 into the concluded face's source vertex M001), so there is no edge in the produced statement playing the analogous epi role gold requires.

Even setting aside the false-epi issue, the natural derivation from the 5 given squares only yields (f ≫ h) ≫ φ_d = (g ≫ k) ≫ φ_d, which would require φ_d to be Mono (not Epi h) to conclude f ≫ h = g ≫ k — confirming the hypothesis choice is mathematically wrong for this face arrangement.
